video_title: So What Happens Next With Kristaps Porzingis & Warriors?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Kristaps Porzingis steps away from basketball due to health concerns
quotes.excerpt: I've made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Since we did our last podcast, there was the development with Kristaps Porzingis where he put out a statement. He's not announcing his retirement, but it's effectively announced his retirement.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: I was going to say, it's effectively announced his retirement. It's definitely a, 'Hey, don't hold your breath for me to be back on the floor.'

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors and union not challenging Kristaps Porzingis's salary status
quotes.excerpt: The heat, he and the union are not challenging him not getting paid.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The fascinating thing about this is that he and the union are not challenging him not getting paid. But his contract theoretically still counts as the 20 million in a trade.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: I do wonder at some point if the union gets involved on that. I also wonder if the league office is going to chime in at all because that's not the spirit of the trade rules.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Kristaps Porzingis's contract functions as a potential trade exception
quotes.excerpt: It essentially functions as a trade exception, and not even that because a trade exception allows you to acquire the player.
quotes.quote: It essentially functions as a trade exception, and not even that because a trade exception allows you to acquire the player. When you trade for a player, and it depends on what team is making the trade because different teams have different rules based on where they are on the aprons, but you can get up to 125 percent of the salary back. It could be a 25 million dollar trade exception that just exists because that's the thing about trade exception, you could just trade for a player, acquire the player, and the other team doesn't have to pay. I wouldn't be surprised if they are considering exactly what you did because this was not, and I don't think the Warriors knew this. I think the Warriors were expecting him to report to camp.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors expected Kristaps Porzingis to report to training camp
quotes.excerpt: The expectation was, okay, Kristaps Porzingis is going to be our starting center for 50-ish games.
quotes.quote: Yes. This was, he went to that little kind of informal voluntary minicamp. He apparently wasn't on the floor, wasn't doing physical stuff, but like he was there. And the expectation was, okay, Kristaps Porzingis is going to be our starting center for 50-ish games, and hopefully, if they made the playoffs, be available then. It wasn't just a one-year deal, it was only 3 million guaranteed next year, but the contract was intentionally signed to be very tradeable and also instantly tradeable, the way it was signed with no raise. But he absolutely factored into their plans.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Kristaps Porzingis's contract helps Warriors stay under the tax
quotes.excerpt: If Kristaps Porzingis's contract is just poof off the books, they could easily duck under the tax.
quotes.quote: This, the Porzingis number takes them right up to the second apron. I'm looking at our Bobby Marks numbers here. They are 347 grand and change from the second apron. Interestingly, they are 20,410,000 over the tax. So if Kristaps Porzingis's contract is just poof off the books, they could easily duck under the tax.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors have three tradable first-round picks to upgrade roster
quotes.excerpt: They do have three tradable first-round picks. They've got their own pick every year moving forward except for 2030.
quotes.quote: They're exploring, searching for ways to use that to upgrade the roster now. We've talked about kind of the different ways to do that. They do have three tradable first-round picks. They've got their own pick every year moving forward except for 2030, which they've got it top-20 protected owed to Memphis. So they can trade up to three first-round picks if they wanted to take a big swing. And again, you got to factor in how much are you willing to go in on this season in Steph's twilight versus how much do you want to have a bridge to the future with Kuminga as a potential face of the franchise.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors could target Jimmy Butler at the trade deadline
quotes.excerpt: Our big trade deadline acquisition is Jimmy Butler.
quotes.quote: I could absolutely see a scenario where they don't make a big swing in the trade market, and February 11, trade deadline comes and goes, and Mike Dunleavy is up there doing his press conference, and then he says, 'Our big trade deadline acquisition is Jimmy Butler.' Because they are hoping, I think planning even, for Jimmy Butler to be back in the mix right around that time.
